entry.title: News Summary: November 25, 2026
entry.summary: Releases: Hermes Agent v0.23.4 is the headline — stable shipped 2026-11-23, consolidating ~229 merged PRs since v0.23.3 into the biggest patch drop of the cycle. Desktop users can also grab the canary.20261124T064706Z canary (macOS/Windows, smoke tests green) for an early look ahead. The rc.2-v0.23.4 and rc.1-v0.23.4 tags landed in the same window but are effectively superseded by stable — pipeline housekeeping only. Tips: Best community contribution this cycle: a tutorial wiring Hermes Agent into an automated PR-review chain (GitHub CLI, linters, governance checks) — directly actionable for dev users. Community: A seven-course roundup ranks the author's own product #1 — self-promotional, use with a caveat or skip; a docs commit refreshing the Hermes Helper Reddit post index is routine maintenance. Bottom three are cut candidates for a tight issue.

entry.title: News Summary: November 24, 2026
entry.summary: Releases: Same-day Hermes Agent canary.20261123T065600Z-v0.23.3 build ships with smoke-tested desktop downloads for macOS (Apple Silicon) and Windows — the headline look at what's headed to stable. Merged PRs: A systemic fix stops Google Chat, Feishu, and Matrix adapters (8 writer code paths) from recreating deleted or renamed profile homes via raw mkdir; a Matrix adapter fix unblocks operator recovery-key output paths outside profile homes on Windows; and a restored Google Chat test assertion re-protects the dead-home regression class. Community: An observability tutorial covers tracing, debugging, and monitoring Hermes Agent runs with observer hooks plus Langfuse, NeMo Relay, and OpenTelemetry. Tips: A practical Discord vs Telegram gateway comparison helps new users pick the right chat setup — Telegram for a phone-first personal line, Discord for richer server-based workflows.

entry.title: News Summary: November 23, 2026
entry.summary: In the news: MarkTechPost's late-2026 buyer's guide names Hermes Agent among the top personal AI agents, compared against OpenClaw and Gemini Spark on memory, security, and cost — strong third-party validation worth sharing. Community plugins: hermes-tenuo brings warrant-based, least-privilege tool authorization to Hermes Agent — signed, expiring warrants restrict which tool calls and arguments can execute; a practical hardening step for anyone running tool-using agents. Integrations: Open-Agent-API exposes agents behind an OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini-compatible gateway (agent ID as the model value), making Hermes-listed agents reachable via standard SDKs. Theme of the week: controlling what agents are allowed to do — authorization, sandboxing, and approval pauses for sensitive actions.
